title: Baby Animals!
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Milo the bluebird, and welcome to The Animated Zoo!
Today we're meeting animal babies, and the families who take care of them!
Can you count five animals with me? One, two, three, four, five!

lines: Here's our first animal. Here's a clue: it's a big, gentle ape with long, strong arms! Can you guess?
Let's swing over to the gorillas!
Gorillas live in green forests, and they eat lots of plants and fruit.
A baby gorilla is tiny. It weighs about four pounds, like a small bag of flour.
Can you make big, strong arms like a gorilla? Strong arms!
Can you guess where a baby gorilla likes to ride?
On mom's back! A piggyback ride through the forest.
Baby gorillas can ride on mom until they are about three or four years old.
And every night, gorillas make a brand-new bed of leaves, called a nest.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's big and gray, with a horn on its nose! Can you guess?
Let's stomp over to the rhinos!
A rhino's horn is made of keratin. That's the same stuff as your fingernails!
Can you wiggle your fingers? Wiggle, wiggle!
Rhinos love to roll in mud. The mud helps keep off the sun and the bugs.
Can you guess how soon a baby rhino can stand up?
In just two or three hours! It's a little wobbly at first.
A baby rhino is called a calf.
Its mom takes care of it for a few years, until it's all grown up.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has whiskers and flippers, and it loves the sea! Can you guess?
Let's splash over to the harbor seals!
Harbor seals rest on rocks and beaches, then slide into the water to swim.
A baby seal is called a pup.
Can you wiggle like a seal on a rock? Wiggle, wiggle!
Can you guess? Can a baby seal swim on the day it is born?
Yes! Harbor seal pups can swim right away, on their very first day.
Let's say it together: HARBOR SEAL!
When it's just a few days old, a pup can dive under the water for up to two minutes!
Pups drink their mom's milk, and they grow fast.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has a long trunk and big ears! Can you guess?
Let's stomp over to the elephants!
Elephants live in families called herds.
A baby elephant is called a calf. It can weigh more than a grown-up person!
Can you stomp like a baby elephant? Stomp, stomp!
Can you guess who helps take care of a baby elephant?
The whole family! Moms, aunts and big sisters all help.
A baby elephant can stand up and drink milk soon after it's born.
Our last animal moves very, very slowly in the trees! Can you guess?
Let's go see the sloths. Slowly!
Sloths sleep for about fifteen hours in the daytime!
Then they wake up at night to eat leaves.
Can you stretch slowly, like a sleepy sloth? Stretch!
Can you guess where a baby sloth holds on?
To mom's tummy! A baby sloth hugs its mom's belly.
It holds on for about five weeks, until it's strong enough to move by itself.
A baby sloth is a little shorter than a ruler.

recap: What a cozy adventure! Let's remember.
Baby gorillas ride on mom's back.
Baby rhinos stand up in just a few hours.
Harbor seal pups can swim on their first day.
The whole elephant family helps with the baby.
And baby sloths hug mom's tummy!
outro: Which baby animal was your favorite? Remember, be kind to every animal. Watch quietly and give them space.
Bye, friends! See you at the zoo!
